slides.0.title: Port and Madeira
slides.0.subtitle: One keeps its fruit in bottle; the other becomes immortal through heat and oxygen
slides.1.title: The Douro and Port winemaking
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Terroir
slides.1.highlights.0.content: A steep schist valley with a hot, dry continental climate; vines on terraces (socalcos, patamares) or planted up the slope (vinha ao alto). Baixo Corgo is coolest and wettest, Cima Corgo the top-quality heart, Douro Superior hottest and driest
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Varieties
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Touriga Nacional (concentration, florality), Touriga Franca (aroma, structure), Tinta Roriz (Tempranillo), Tinta Barroca, Tinto Cão and others, usually field-blended and co-fermented
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Fast extraction and fortification
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Because fermentation runs only two or three days before fortification, extraction must be fast: traditionally foot-treading in stone lagares, now robotic treading or autovinifiers; grape spirit (aguardente) at about 77% is added, roughly one part spirit to four of wine
slides.1.content: Port winemaking logic: short fermentation → extraction must be intense → to gain colour and tannin.
slides.2.title: Ruby and Tawny
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The Ruby family (reductive)
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Ruby and Reserve age briefly in large vats; LBV is bottled after 4–6 years in wood; Vintage Port is declared only in fine years, bottled after about two years and ages for decades in bottle
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The Tawny family (oxidative)
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Long oxidative ageing in small casks (pipes); 10-, 20-, 30- and 40-year indications describe the average style; Colheita is a single-vintage Tawny aged at least 7 years in wood
slides.2.highlights.2.title: White and Pink Port
slides.2.highlights.2.content: White Port uses white grapes, from dry to sweet, and is often mixed with tonic; Pink Port is made with short skin contact, aimed at younger drinkers and cocktails
slides.2.content: Vintage Port and Colheita both carry a vintage, but one ages reductively in bottle and the other oxidatively in cask.
slides.3.title: Madeira
slides.3.highlights.0.title: History and heat
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Madeira once crossed the tropics in ships’ holds, and people found heat improved it, so heated ageing developed; this makes Madeira almost immune to oxidation and long-lived even after opening
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Varieties and sweetness
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The four noble varieties from dry to sweet: Sercial, Verdelho, Boal (Bual) and Malvasia (Malmsey); the later the fortification, the drier the wine. The most widely planted is the versatile Tinta Negra
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Vintage and age indications
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Age indications such as 5, 10, 15 and 20 years; Colheita is single-vintage with at least 5 years’ ageing; Frasqueira (Vintage) spends at least 20 years in cask and is the top tier
slides.3.content: Madeira’s keywords: heat, oxidation, high acidity, which is why it is almost immortal.
